entries.title: Finite critical two-point operator norm implies a nonuniqueness phase on a Cayley graph
entries.statement: Let G be an infinite countable vertex-transitive graph of bounded degree with Bernoulli bond percolation, adjacency operator A on l2(V), a=||A||>0, and critical threshold p_c<1. If the two-point kernel T_{p_c}(x,y)=P_{p_c}(x connected to y) defines a bounded l2 operator with norm M<infinity, then for p_c<=q<min(1,p_c+1/(aM)), ||T_q||<=M/[1-aM(q-p_c)]. Consequently p_c<p_{2->2}<=p_u.
entries.proof_text: In each finite induced subgraph, Russo's formula expresses the derivative of connection probability as the sum of pivotal-edge probabilities. Pivotality after deleting an edge forces disjoint paths in one of the two orientations. BK bounds the derivative entrywise by T_p A T_p. Thus f(p)=||T_p|| satisfies f'<=a f^2 almost everywhere and f(p_c)<=M; integration gives the displayed bound, uniformly in finite volume. Exhaustion gives the full-graph bound by monotone convergence of connection events and bounded bilinear forms. If a unique infinite cluster existed at a bounded-kernel parameter, transitivity gives theta>0 and FKG gives T_p(x,y)>=theta^2 for all vertices, so a kernel column could not be in l2. Hence p_{2->2}<=p_u.
assumptions: T_{p_c} is bounded on counting-measure l2(V) with norm M

entries.title: C0047 spectral criterion needs the degree factor
entries.statement: For a d-regular Cayley graph, if rho is the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius, the Benjamini-Schramm sufficient criterion is d*rho*p_c<1. The earlier C0047 attempt's p_c<1/rho drops d; when 0<rho<1 this inequality is automatic because p_c<=1<1/rho, so it cannot certify p_c<p_u. The corrected criterion is only sufficient: on the four-regular tree p_c=1/3, rho=sqrt(3)/2 and d*rho*p_c=2sqrt(3)/3>1 although p_u=1.
assumptions: rho=||A||/d is the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius

relations.rationale: The existing problem card asks p_c<p_u for every nonamenable Cayley graph; this reviewed lemma gives that inequality only when the critical two-point operator is bounded, leaving that assumption explicit.

The stored attempt says p_c<1/rho for normalized random-walk rho; this correction states the source criterion d*rho*p_c<1 and supplies the four-regular-tree counterexample to the missing-factor route.
